## Statement refuted

**Assume Countable Choice.** The false statement is: weak convergence in the periodic solenoidal space $H$
alone guarantees weak convergence of the quadratic tensors $u_n\otimes u_n$
to $u\otimes u$.

## Statement references

[Leonid Ryzhik, *Math 256B Lecture Notes*, §§5.3–5.4, pp. 43–48](https://virtualmath1.stanford.edu/~ryzhik/notes-256B-24.pdf).

[Berselli and Spirito, *On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions*, §4, pp. 8–12](https://www.mdpi.com/2311-5521/6/1/42/pdf).

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable Choice, the normalized torus $\mathbb T_L^d$, an integer $d\ge2$, and the Fourier and solenoidal conventions of [[def-fd-periodic-solenoidal-spaces]].

[F1] [[def-fd-periodic-solenoidal-spaces]]: a vector field with Fourier support at $\pm k$ and coefficients perpendicular to $k$ is in $H$; its $H$ norm is the Parseval norm.

[F2] [[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]]: under Countable Choice, trigonometric polynomials are dense in $L^2$ and Fourier coefficients give its complete orthonormal expansion.

## Counterexample

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Fix the second coordinate vector $e_2\in\mathbb R^d$ and set
$$u_n(x)=\sin(2\pi n x_1/L)e_2,\qquad u(x)=0.$$
Each $u_n$ has only the Fourier modes $k=\pm ne_1$ and its vector coefficient is perpendicular to $k$, so $u_n\in H$. For a finite trigonometric polynomial $g$, $(u_n,g)_H=0$ for all sufficiently large $n$ because its Fourier support is finite. Approximate an arbitrary $g\in H$ by such polynomials using [F2]; the error is at most $\sup_n\|u_n\|_2$ times the approximation error. Hence $u_n\rightharpoonup0$ in $H$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 The only nonzero entry of $u_n\otimes u_n$ is its $(2,2)$ entry, equal to
$$\sin^2(2\pi n x_1/L)=\tfrac12-\tfrac12\cos(4\pi n x_1/L).$$
The oscillatory cosine has zero pairing eventually with every finite trigonometric polynomial and its $L^2$ norm is uniformly bounded; density and Cauchy–Schwarz therefore show it converges weakly to zero in $L^2$. Thus $u_n\otimes u_n\rightharpoonup\tfrac12 e_2\otimes e_2$ in $L^2$, while $u\otimes u=0$. This refutes the false statement. These fields are only a functional-analytic witness and are not claimed to solve Navier–Stokes. [given, F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement refuted

**Assume Countable Choice.** Fix $d\ge2$ and $L>0$, and let $H$ be the real periodic solenoidal $L^2$ space on $\mathbb T_L^d=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^d$, with normalized Lebesgue measure $d\mu=L^{-d}dx$. The false statement is: if $u_n\rightharpoonup u$ in $H$, then $u_n\otimes u_n\rightharpoonup u\otimes u$ weakly in $L^1(\mathbb T_L^d;\mathbb R^{d\times d})$. Each tensor belongs to $L^1$ because its Frobenius norm is $|u_n|^2$; weak $L^1$ convergence means
$$\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}(u_n\otimes u_n):\Phi\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int_{\mathbb T_L^d}(u\otimes u):\Phi\,d\mu$$
for every essentially bounded measurable real matrix field $\Phi$, where $A:\Phi=\sum_{i,j=1}^dA_{ij}\Phi_{ij}$. Thus the claim concerns arbitrary weakly convergent $H$ fields, without an additional $L^4$ assumption.

## Statement references

[Leonid Ryzhik, *Math 256B Lecture Notes*, §§5.3–5.4, pp. 43–48](https://virtualmath1.stanford.edu/~ryzhik/notes-256B-24.pdf).

[Berselli and Spirito, *On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions*, §4, pp. 8–12](https://www.mdpi.com/2311-5521/6/1/42/pdf).

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable Choice, the normalized torus $\mathbb T_L^d$, an integer $d\ge2$, and the Fourier and solenoidal conventions of [[def-fd-periodic-solenoidal-spaces]].

[F1] [[def-fd-periodic-solenoidal-spaces]]: a vector field with Fourier support at $\pm k$ and coefficients perpendicular to $k$ is in $H$; its $H$ norm is the Parseval norm.

[F2] [[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]]: under Countable Choice, trigonometric polynomials are dense in $L^2$ and Fourier coefficients give its complete orthonormal expansion.

## Counterexample

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Fix the second coordinate vector $e_2\in\mathbb R^d$ and set
$$u_n(x)=\sin(2\pi n x_1/L)e_2,\qquad u(x)=0.$$
Each $u_n$ has only the Fourier modes $k=\pm ne_1$ and its vector coefficient is perpendicular to $k$, so $u_n\in H$. For a finite trigonometric polynomial $g$, $(u_n,g)_H=0$ for all sufficiently large $n$ because its Fourier support is finite. Approximate an arbitrary $g\in H$ by such polynomials using [F2]; the error is at most $\sup_n\|u_n\|_2$ times the approximation error. Hence $u_n\rightharpoonup0$ in $H$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 The only nonzero entry of $u_n\otimes u_n$ is its $(2,2)$ entry, equal to
$$\sin^2(2\pi n x_1/L)=\tfrac12-\tfrac12\cos(4\pi n x_1/L).$$
The oscillatory cosine has zero pairing eventually with every finite trigonometric polynomial and its $L^2$ norm is uniformly bounded; density and Cauchy–Schwarz therefore show it converges weakly to zero in $L^2$. Thus $u_n\otimes u_n\rightharpoonup\tfrac12 e_2\otimes e_2$ in $L^2$. Since the torus measure is one, every essentially bounded matrix test satisfies $\|\Phi\|_2\le\|\Phi\|_\infty$, so this convergence also holds against every weak $L^1$ test. In particular the constant test $\Phi=e_2\otimes e_2$ gives $\int(u_n\otimes u_n):\Phi\,d\mu=1/2$ for every $n$, whereas $\int(u\otimes u):\Phi\,d\mu=0$. Hence the tensors do not converge weakly in $L^1$ to $u\otimes u=0$; the same smooth constant test also rules out convergence to zero as periodic distributions. This refutes the false statement. These fields are only a functional-analytic witness and are not claimed to solve Navier–Stokes. [given, F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be bounded and
open, and let $H,V$ be the closure spaces defined above. There is a constant $C$ independent of $\Omega$
and $a$ such that every $a\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ satisfies
$$\|a\|_{L^6(\Omega)}\le C\|\nabla a\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad \|a\|_{L^4(\Omega)}\le\|a\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^{1/4}\|a\|_{L^6(\Omega)}^{3/4}.$$
For $T>0$, if $u\in L^\infty(0,T;H)\cap L^2(0,T;V)$, then
$u\in L^{8/3}(0,T;L^4(\Omega))$. Here the time-dependent $L^p$ notation
means strong measurability and integrability of the displayed norm; the
continuous embedding $V\to L^4(\Omega)$ carries strongly measurable
$V$-valued maps to strongly measurable $L^4$-valued maps. Let $V^*$ be the
continuous real-linear dual of $V$ with its operator norm and set
$$b_u(t)(\phi)=-\int_\Omega u_i(t,x)u_j(t,x)\partial_j\phi_i(x)dx,\qquad\phi\in V.$$
Then $b_u(t)\in V^*$, $t\mapsto b_u(t)$ is strongly measurable, and
$b_u\in L^{4/3}(0,T;V^*)$ with
$\|b_u(t)\|_{V^*}\le\|u(t)\|_{L^4(\Omega)}^2.$

## Statement references

[Berselli and Spirito, *On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions*, §2.2, p. 5](https://www.mdpi.com/2311-5521/6/1/42/pdf).

[Leonid Ryzhik, *Math 256B Lecture Notes*, §5.2, pp. 39–43](https://virtualmath1.stanford.edu/~ryzhik/notes-256B-24.pdf).

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, a bounded open $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$, $a\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, and $u\in L^\infty(0,T;H)\cap L^2(0,T;V)$ for the closure spaces defined above.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; the basis/separability input below is used under this hypothesis.

[F1] [[def-fd-bounded-solenoidal-spaces]]: $H_0^1$ is the closure of compactly supported smooth fields in the $H^1$ norm; $V$ embeds continuously into $H_0^1$.

[F2] [[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]]: Hölder's inequality includes Cauchy–Schwarz for the integrable products below.

[F3] [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]: the coordinate-line integrals below may be iterated and reordered.

[F4] [[thm-first-fundamental-theorem-of-calculus-for-l-one]]: under Countable Choice, integration of the derivative of a smooth function along a coordinate line recovers its endpoint difference.

[F5] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice selects a Sobolev-approximating sequence from the closure definition of $H_0^1$.

[F6] [[lem-fd-bounded-solenoidal-basis]]: $V$ is a separable Hilbert space and its finite smooth solenoidal span is dense in $V$.

[F7] [[def-fd-weak-time-continuity]]: for a separable Hilbert target, $L^p(0,T;X)$ means strong measurability and an integrable $p$th-power norm.

[F8] [[lem-fd-bounded-dual-separability]]: the Riesz map is a surjective isometry from $V$ onto $V^*$, so $V^*$ is a separable Hilbert space and the Bochner convention in [F7] applies.

## Proof

1.1 For $h\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ define $A_1(x_2,x_3)=\int_{\mathbb R}|\partial_1h(x_1,x_2,x_3)|dx_1$, and define $A_2(x_1,x_3)$ and $A_3(x_1,x_2)$ analogously. By [F4], $|h(x)|\le A_i(x_{\widehat i})$ for each $i$, hence $|h|^{3/2}\le(A_1A_2A_3)^{1/2}$. Put $B_2(x_3)=\int A_2(x_1,x_3)dx_1$ and $B_3(x_2)=\int A_3(x_1,x_2)dx_1$. Cauchy–Schwarz in $x_1$ gives $\int(A_2A_3)^{1/2}dx_1\le(B_2B_3)^{1/2}$; applying Cauchy–Schwarz in $(x_2,x_3)$ to the remaining $A_1^{1/2}(B_2B_3)^{1/2}$ gives
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}|h|^{3/2}\le(\int_{\mathbb R^2}A_1)^{1/2}(\int_{\mathbb R}B_2)^{1/2}(\int_{\mathbb R}B_3)^{1/2}=\prod_{i=1}^3(\int_{\mathbb R^3}|\partial_i h|)^{1/2}.$$
The changes of integration order are justified by [F3]. Raising to the power $2/3$ yields $\|h\|_{3/2}\le\prod_i\|\partial_i h\|_1^{1/3}$. [given, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 For a smooth compactly supported vector field $w$, set $h=|w|^4$, which is smooth, and note $|\partial_i h|\le4|w|^3|\partial_iw|$. Hölder gives $\|\partial_i h\|_1\le4\|w\|_6^3\|\partial_iw\|_2$. Substitution into step 1.1 yields $\|w\|_6^4\le4\|w\|_6^3\prod_i\|\partial_iw\|_2^{1/3}\le4\|w\|_6^3\|\nabla w\|_2$. Divide when $\|w\|_6>0$; if it is zero the inequality is immediate. [given, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 By [F1] and [F5], choose $w_n\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ converging to $a$ in $H^1$. The inequality of step 2.1 applied to differences makes $(w_n)$ Cauchy in $L^6$; on bounded $\Omega$, convergence in $L^6$ also implies convergence in $L^2$, so its $L^6$ limit is the given $L^2$ class $a$. Passing to the limit proves the first inequality. Finally, $\int|a|^4\le(\int|a|^2)^{1/2}(\int|a|^6)^{1/2}$ by Cauchy–Schwarz, which proves the interpolation inequality. For almost every $t$, raising it to power $8/3$ gives $\|u(t)\|_4^{8/3}\le\|u(t)\|_2^{2/3}\|u(t)\|_6^2\le C\|u(t)\|_H^{2/3}\|u(t)\|_V^2$. Integrating and using $u\in L^\infty_tH\cap L^2_tV$ proves the stated $L^{8/3}_tL^4_x$ bound. [given, F1, F2, F5, step 2.1]

4.1 For each time, Hölder gives $|b_u(t)(\phi)|\le\|u(t)\|_4^2\|\nabla\phi\|_2$, so $b_u(t)\in V^*$ and its norm is at most $\|u(t)\|_4^2$. The map $a\mapsto b_a$ is continuous from $L^4$ to $V^*$ because $\|b_a-b_c\|_{V^*}\le(\|a\|_4+\|c\|_4)\|a-c\|_4$. The continuous embedding and strong measurability of $u$ in $V$ therefore give strong measurability of $t\mapsto b_u(t)$ in the separable Hilbert space $V^*$ by [F6,F8]. Finally $\int_0^T\|b_u(t)\|_{V^*}^{4/3}dt\le\int_0^T\|u(t)\|_4^{8/3}dt<\infty$ by step 3.1; [F7] gives $b_u\in L^{4/3}(0,T;V^*)$. [given, A1, F2, F6, F7, F8, step 3.1] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be bounded and
open, and let $H,V$ be the closure spaces defined above. There is a constant $C$ independent of $\Omega$
and $a$ such that every $a\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ satisfies
$$\|a\|_{L^6(\Omega)}\le C\|\nabla a\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad \|a\|_{L^4(\Omega)}\le\|a\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^{1/4}\|a\|_{L^6(\Omega)}^{3/4}.$$
For $T>0$, if $u\in L^\infty(0,T;H)\cap L^2(0,T;V)$, then
$u\in L^{8/3}(0,T;L^4(\Omega))$. Here the time-dependent $L^p$ notation
means strong measurability and integrability of the displayed norm; the
continuous embedding $V\to L^4(\Omega)$ carries strongly measurable
$V$-valued maps to strongly measurable $L^4$-valued maps. Let $V^*$ be the
continuous real-linear dual of $V$ with its operator norm. Choose any strongly measurable representative $\widetilde u:(0,T)\to V$ of the $L^2(0,T;V)$ class of $u$; through the embedding $V\to H$, it represents the same $H$-valued class almost everywhere. For almost every $t\in(0,T)$ define
$$b_u(t)(\phi)=-\int_\Omega \widetilde u_i(t,x)\widetilde u_j(t,x)\partial_j\phi_i(x)dx,\qquad\phi\in V,$$
and assign $b_u(t)=0$ on any exceptional null set. Then $b_u(t)\in V^*$ for almost every $t$, $t\mapsto b_u(t)$ is strongly measurable, and its equivalence class is independent of the chosen representative $\widetilde u$. This class belongs to $L^{4/3}(0,T;V^*)$ and satisfies
$$\|b_u(t)\|_{V^*}\le\|\widetilde u(t)\|_{L^4(\Omega)}^2\quad\text{for almost every }t\in(0,T).$$

## Statement references

[Berselli and Spirito, *On the Existence of Leray–Hopf Weak Solutions*, §2.2, p. 5](https://www.mdpi.com/2311-5521/6/1/42/pdf).

[Leonid Ryzhik, *Math 256B Lecture Notes*, §5.2, pp. 39–43](https://virtualmath1.stanford.edu/~ryzhik/notes-256B-24.pdf).

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, a bounded open $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$, $a\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, and $u\in L^\infty(0,T;H)\cap L^2(0,T;V)$ for the closure spaces defined above.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; the basis/separability input below is used under this hypothesis.

[F1] [[def-fd-bounded-solenoidal-spaces]]: $H_0^1$ is the closure of compactly supported smooth fields in the $H^1$ norm; $V$ embeds continuously into $H_0^1$.

[F2] [[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]]: Hölder's inequality includes Cauchy–Schwarz for the integrable products below.

[F3] [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]: the coordinate-line integrals below may be iterated and reordered.

[F4] [[thm-first-fundamental-theorem-of-calculus-for-l-one]]: under Countable Choice, integration of the derivative of a smooth function along a coordinate line recovers its endpoint difference.

[F5] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice selects a Sobolev-approximating sequence from the closure definition of $H_0^1$.

[F6] [[lem-fd-bounded-solenoidal-basis]]: $V$ is a separable Hilbert space and its finite smooth solenoidal span is dense in $V$.

[F7] [[def-fd-weak-time-continuity]]: for a separable Hilbert target, $L^p(0,T;X)$ means strong measurability and an integrable $p$th-power norm.

[F8] [[lem-fd-bounded-dual-separability]]: the Riesz map is a surjective isometry from $V$ onto $V^*$, so $V^*$ is a separable Hilbert space and the Bochner convention in [F7] applies.

## Proof

1.1 For $h\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ define $A_1(x_2,x_3)=\int_{\mathbb R}|\partial_1h(x_1,x_2,x_3)|dx_1$, and define $A_2(x_1,x_3)$ and $A_3(x_1,x_2)$ analogously. By [F4], $|h(x)|\le A_i(x_{\widehat i})$ for each $i$, hence $|h|^{3/2}\le(A_1A_2A_3)^{1/2}$. Put $B_2(x_3)=\int A_2(x_1,x_3)dx_1$ and $B_3(x_2)=\int A_3(x_1,x_2)dx_1$. Cauchy–Schwarz in $x_1$ gives $\int(A_2A_3)^{1/2}dx_1\le(B_2B_3)^{1/2}$; applying Cauchy–Schwarz in $(x_2,x_3)$ to the remaining $A_1^{1/2}(B_2B_3)^{1/2}$ gives
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}|h|^{3/2}\le(\int_{\mathbb R^2}A_1)^{1/2}(\int_{\mathbb R}B_2)^{1/2}(\int_{\mathbb R}B_3)^{1/2}=\prod_{i=1}^3(\int_{\mathbb R^3}|\partial_i h|)^{1/2}.$$
The changes of integration order are justified by [F3]. Raising to the power $2/3$ yields $\|h\|_{3/2}\le\prod_i\|\partial_i h\|_1^{1/3}$. [given, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 For a smooth compactly supported vector field $w$, set $h=|w|^4$, which is smooth, and note $|\partial_i h|\le4|w|^3|\partial_iw|$. Hölder gives $\|\partial_i h\|_1\le4\|w\|_6^3\|\partial_iw\|_2$. Substitution into step 1.1 yields $\|w\|_6^4\le4\|w\|_6^3\prod_i\|\partial_iw\|_2^{1/3}\le4\|w\|_6^3\|\nabla w\|_2$. Divide when $\|w\|_6>0$; if it is zero the inequality is immediate. [given, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 By [F1] and [F5], choose $w_n\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ converging to $a$ in $H^1$. The inequality of step 2.1 applied to differences makes $(w_n)$ Cauchy in $L^6$; on bounded $\Omega$, convergence in $L^6$ also implies convergence in $L^2$, so its $L^6$ limit is the given $L^2$ class $a$. Passing to the limit proves the first inequality. Finally, $\int|a|^4\le(\int|a|^2)^{1/2}(\int|a|^6)^{1/2}$ by Cauchy–Schwarz, which proves the interpolation inequality. For almost every $t$, raising it to power $8/3$ gives $\|u(t)\|_4^{8/3}\le\|u(t)\|_2^{2/3}\|u(t)\|_6^2\le C\|u(t)\|_H^{2/3}\|u(t)\|_V^2$. Integrating and using $u\in L^\infty_tH\cap L^2_tV$ proves the stated $L^{8/3}_tL^4_x$ bound. [given, F1, F2, F5, step 2.1]

4.1 Fix the strongly measurable representative $\widetilde u$ chosen in the Statement. For almost every time, Hölder gives $|b_u(t)(\phi)|\le\|\widetilde u(t)\|_4^2\|\nabla\phi\|_2$, so $b_u(t)\in V^*$ and its norm is at most $\|\widetilde u(t)\|_4^2$. The map $a\mapsto b_a$ is continuous from $L^4$ to $V^*$ because $\|b_a-b_c\|_{V^*}\le(\|a\|_4+\|c\|_4)\|a-c\|_4$. Composing simple-map approximations to $\widetilde u$ with the continuous embedding $V\to L^4$ and this map therefore gives strongly measurable $V^*$-valued $b_u$, up to the permitted null-set assignment; [F6,F8] provide the separable Hilbert target. Two representatives of the same $L^2_tV$ class agree in $V$ almost everywhere, hence agree in $L^4$ there and define the same $b_u$ almost everywhere. Thus its Bochner class is independent of the representative. Finally $\int_0^T\|b_u(t)\|_{V^*}^{4/3}dt\le\int_0^T\|\widetilde u(t)\|_4^{8/3}dt<\infty$ by step 3.1; [F7] gives $b_u\in L^{4/3}(0,T;V^*)$. [given, A1, F2, F6, F7, F8, step 3.1] ∎

findings.confirmed_defect: The refuted assertion omitted the topology on quadratic tensors even though general H products are only L1.
findings.resolution: Specified weak L1 tensor convergence for the full d>=2 periodic H class and defined its bounded-matrix test pairing. Retained the oscillatory witness and its stronger weak L2 limit; proved the probability-volume L-infinity-to-L2 bridge and constant-test failure of convergence to u tensor u.

findings.confirmed_defect: A Bochner equivalence class was used to define b_u(t) and its dual membership at each time without selecting a representative.
findings.resolution: Select any strongly measurable V-valued representative of the L2_tV class;define the nonlinear functional a.e.,assign zero on exceptional null sets,and assert the norm bound a.e. The proof establishes strong measurability,representative independence of the resulting V*-valued class,and the identical L4/3 integrability.

cex-fd-weak-products: All weakly convergent real solenoidal H sequences remain in the false assertion; no extra L4,boundedness,smoothness or equation-solving hypothesis was imposed on them.
The parameter scope is the same normalized torus with arbitrary d>=2 and L>0 already present in the original Given paragraph.
Each general tensor has L1 Frobenius norm equal to the squared L2 velocity norm,so the selected weak L1 topology is defined on the entire announced class.

The same witness sin(2pi n x1/L)e2 has weak H limit zero and weak L2 tensor limit one-half e2 tensor e2. Every bounded tensor test is L2 because the normalized volume is one,so that witness also has the displayed weak L1 limit.

The single constant smooth test e2 tensor e2 has tensor integral one-half for every n and zero against the claimed limiting product;this directly disproves both weak L1 convergence and distributional convergence to zero.
Countable Choice and the original Fourier/Parseval dependencies are preserved;no new premise is imported.
lem-fd-no-slip-lsix: The Axiom of Choice and its original Countable Choice,Sobolev,Fubini/Holder,FTC and separability suppliers remain unchanged.
The arbitrary bounded open R3 domain,no-slip closure spaces and all original zero-boundary L6/L4 estimates are preserved. No boundary smoothness or pointwise trace is added.
The original energy-space input L-infinity_tH intersect L2_tV and conclusions L8/3_tL4_x and L4/3_tV* retain exactly their exponents and full time-interval range.
Choosing a strongly measurable V representative is licensed by the already-declared Bochner convention;it is not an extra regularity assumption. Its H image is the same equivalence class a.e.

The continuity bound ||b_a-b_c||<= (||a||4+||c||4)||a-c||4 maps simple representative approximations into strongly measurable V*-valued approximations. Equal V representatives agree in L4 a.e.,hence yield identical dual-valued classes.
The original integrated inequality for ||b_u||^(4/3) is unchanged;no output depending on a particular null-set value survives.
